options.text: The splitting of a large nucleus into two smaller nuclei
The joining of two small nuclei to form a larger nucleus, releasing energy
The emission of gamma radiation from a nucleus
The absorption of neutrons by a nucleus

questions.explanation: Nuclear fusion is the process in which two small, light nuclei join together to form a larger nucleus, releasing a large amount of energy in the process. It is the process that powers stars, including our Sun, where hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium.

questions.stem: Why does nuclear fusion require extremely high temperatures?

options.text: To overcome the electrostatic repulsion between the positively charged nuclei
To break the nuclei apart before they can fuse
To increase the mass of the nuclei

questions.explanation: Both nuclei are positively charged (they contain protons), so they repel each other. Extremely high temperatures (millions of degrees) give the nuclei enough kinetic energy to overcome this electrostatic repulsion and get close enough for the strong nuclear force to bind them together.
